facts.statement: The `ignore-paths` option is defined as a list of path regular expressions, defaults to an empty list, and is documented to accept either POSIX or Windows path formats.
The `recursive` option defaults to false and is documented as discovering Python modules and packages in a filesystem subtree.
TOML configuration parsing reads values below `tool.pylint`; nested tables such as `tool.pylint.MASTER` are flattened into command-line-style option/value arguments.
Configuration-file options are parsed before command-line options, and command-line options can override configuration-file values.
Path-regex configuration values are transformed into a compiled alternation containing Windows-style and POSIX-style forms of each supplied pattern.
Ignore regex matching uses `Pattern.match`, so matching starts at the beginning of the candidate string unless the configured expression itself permits a prefix.
A path is considered ignored when its basename is in `ignore`, its basename matches `ignore-patterns`, or its full candidate string matches `ignore-paths`.
Recursive discovery walks non-package directory arguments and applies all three ignore mechanisms to each walked directory root; an ignored root is recorded so its subtree is skipped.
For walked directories that are not packages, recursive discovery yields every filename ending in `.py` without applying an ignore check at that yield site.
When recursive mode is enabled, discovery runs before the resulting files or modules enter the normal checking pipeline.
The normal expansion stage again receives `ignore`, `ignore-patterns`, and the linter's stored `ignore-paths` collection.
Module expansion rejects an explicitly supplied or recursively discovered candidate immediately when `_is_ignored_file` matches it.
Existing end-to-end recursive-ignore tests cover `--ignore-paths` only as command-line arguments, using broad expressions `.*ignored.*` and `.*failing.*`.
The lower-level parameterized recursive-ignore test also supplies ignore settings on the command line and uses unanchored `ignore-paths` expressions beginning with `.*`.
Configuration tests verify that configured `ignore-paths` expressions match both forward-slash and backslash paths.
Existing module-expansion coverage for non-default `ignore-paths` uses the unanchored expression `.*/lint/.*`.

scope_summary: Inspected the supplied repository at base commit 3c5eca2ded3dd2b59ebaf23eb289453b5d2930f0. Relevant existing behavior spans configuration parsing, path-regex transformation, recursive discovery, ignore matching, and recursive-ignore tests.
unknowns: The repository contains no cited test combining recursive discovery, a TOML-provided `ignore-paths` value, and an expression anchored to a relative path such as `^src/gen/.*$`.

The inspected code does not establish which exact candidate path spelling `os.walk` produces for the reported Windows invocation; that runtime detail determines whether an anchored relative expression matches during directory discovery.
